clue.text: Awful high-class lot tend for the most part to be in command

indicators.note: awful says the letters that follow are in a dreadful state and must be put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

indicators.note: for the most part keeps most of the word before it, dropping only its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before it loses a letter

explanation.surface: A dreadful crowd of aristocrats usually end up running things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' trims 'tend' to TEN, and 'Awful' rearranges that together with 'high-class lot'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: whoever gives the orders and makes the decisions is the one in charge.

clue.text: With nothing to hold on to, suffer evil attack

indicators.note: on to attaches the piece built from evil after the suffering word

parts.note: to incur a loss is to suffer it

indicators.note: to hold means the evil word has the nothing letter inside it

parts.note: sin is evil, wrongdoing
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone with no handhold is struck by a wicked assault.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'hold on to' as one phrase, but it splits in two: 'to hold' is the insertion and 'on to' the join.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a sudden raid or invasion into another's territory.

clue.text: Apply, even after setback

indicators.note: the word still says the same thing even after being set back, that is, written in the opposite direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Put in an application, even following a disappointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even after setback' tells you the answer is unchanged when written backwards, a palindrome; there are no other pieces to find.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in the sense of relating to: a rule that applies to members pertains to them.

clue.text: Manfully oppose monster, sticking end of spear in

indicators.note: sticking, with in, says a letter is pushed inside the monster word
in completes sticking ... in: the letter goes inside the monster

parts.note: a beast is a monster

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word that follows it

explanation.surface: A hero bravely confronts a monster, driving the spear point home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' takes R from 'spear', and 'sticking … in' pushes it inside BEAST.
explanation.definitionFit: To breast waves or a hill is to meet it boldly, chest first.

clue.text: Happen to see heavenly body by street in Paris

indicators.note: by places the first piece beside the second, in clue order

parts.note: a comet is a body orbiting the sun
rue is the French word for street

explanation.surface: Chancing to spot a star above a Parisian road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happen to see' reads as one phrase, but only 'Happen' is the definition; 'by' simply sets the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A wish or prediction that is realised is said to do this; a synonym for materialise.

clue.text: Sober, having tossed drink back into river

indicators.note: into places the turned drink inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland, and another on the Welsh border

indicators.note: tossed, with back, says the drink is thrown the other way round
back completes tossed ... back: the drink's letters run from last to first

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a drink

explanation.surface: A newly abstinent person has thrown their drink away into the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sober' suggests abstinence but means sedate. 'tossed … back' gives MUR, which 'into' places within the name of a British river.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a modest, serious, restrained manner, as in sober dress.

clue.text: This person with bombast about church — one with story on pilgrimage?

indicators.note: with joins the first piece to what follows it

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself is me

indicators.note: about means the bombast word goes round the church letters

parts.note: a rant is loud, inflated talk, bombast

explanation.surface: The speaker is holding forth pompously on religion, like a pilgrim with a tale to tell.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to Chaucer's Canterbury Tales, where each pilgrim tells a story on the road. 'about' is the insertion, and 'with' joins the setter to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader is one of the pilgrims who tells a tale in Chaucer's Canterbury Tales.

clue.text: Did store flog red range?

indicators.note: to flog is to beat, so the letters after it are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Was a shop selling off its scarlet cookers?
explanation.walkthrough: 'store' poses as a noun, a shop; it is a verb, and 'Did store' is a past-tense definition. 'flog', British slang for sell, is the anagram signal in its beating sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To garner is to gather and lay up, as grain in a granary, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: Bringer about of employment positioned to drive off maybe

indicators.note: positioned says where the employment word sits: placed within the vehicle, like a motorist

parts.note: a car is what you might be sitting in to drive off
use is employment, as in the use of force

explanation.surface: A creator of jobs stands on the tee, perhaps, ready to hit the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'positioned to drive off maybe' is a whimsical way of saying 'in a motor vehicle', so 'positioned' is the insertion. The surface hints at golf.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent noun: whatever produces or occasions something is what brings it about.

clue.text: A body-builder with the shape of a star

definitions.text: with the shape of a star

parts.note: a steroid is a drug taken to build muscle, so whimsically a builder of bodies

explanation.surface: A muscleman whose physique has five points.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems to describe a person, and the answer is better known as a body in space; the definition is its rarer adjective sense. The body-builder is a drug, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word literally means star-like, from the Greek aster.

clue.text: Woodlouse maybe is found at front of old school

indicators.note: found at front of puts the word is ahead of the two pieces that follow it

parts.note: O is an abbreviation for old, as in OT, Old Testament
a pod is a school of whales or dolphins

explanation.surface: A small bug turns up outside the former schoolhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old school' reads as one thing but gives two pieces, and the school is of whales. 'found at front of' sets IS before them.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodlouse is an example of this order of crustaceans with equal legs.

clue.text: Person to celebrate

definitions.meaning: in legal language, an individual involved in a contract or case
as a verb, to make merry at a festive gathering

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a legal term for an individual and, as a verb, means to revel.

clue.text: Journey by European across Germany's western border — one may be in tent

indicators.note: by sets the journey word next to the European
across means the joined pieces span the single letter, which sits inside them

parts.note: a ride is a journey on horseback or in a vehicle

indicators.note: on a map west is the left, so this is the left-hand edge letter of the word before it

parts.note: a Pole is a native of Poland

explanation.surface: A trip alongside a European over the German frontier, perhaps sleeping under canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'western border' takes G from the left edge of 'Germany's'; 'by' joins RIDE and POLE, and 'across' has them span that G.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the horizontal bar along the top of a tent that holds up the canvas.

clue.text: Go into declaration made by arm of US Government

indicators.note: into sends the going word inside the declaration word

parts.note: a statement is a declaration
to go is to depart

explanation.surface: Examine an announcement issued by a branch of the American administration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go into' reads as 'examine', but the two words split apart: 'into' is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the federal ministry that handles America's foreign affairs.

clue.text: Lifted two items of furniture for chambers upstairs?

parts.words: two items of furniture for chambers upstairs?
parts.note: a crib is a baby's cot, kept in a bedroom, a chamber upstairs

parts.words: two items of furniture for chambers upstairs?
parts.note: the other bedroom furnishing is what an adult sleeps on, a bed

explanation.surface: Two pieces of furniture were carried up for the upper rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifted' looks like carrying furniture upstairs; it means plagiarised. The 'chambers upstairs' are bedrooms, where both items belong.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are slang for copying someone else's work, as a cheating pupil does.

clue.text: What's said to be filthy and terribly cruel

indicators.note: terribly says the word beside it is in a bad state, its letters disordered

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Something reputedly disgusting and dreadfully unkind.
explanation.definitionFit: Money is proverbially called filthy in this fixed phrase, which comes from the King James Bible.

clue.text: Trendy book on the must-read-one-day list?

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: A fashionable novel sitting on the pile to be read eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' looks like the noun the definition goes on to talk about; it is the verb, as in booking a table.
explanation.definitionFit: A whimsical example: something kept back for later is set aside like reading you mean to get round to.

clue.text: Disagreeable filth editor's first got rid of

indicators.note: got rid of means that letter is dropped from the filth word

parts.note: grime is ingrained dirt

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: The editor's top priority was removing the nasty smut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes E from 'editor's', and 'got rid of' drops it from GRIME.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: both mean unpleasant or forbidding, as in a bleak prospect.

clue.text: Good to see in royal house something surviving from the past

indicators.note: to see in tells you the letter is found inside the dynasty's name

parts.note: Hanover was the British royal house from George I to Victoria
G is an abbreviation for good, as in grading

explanation.surface: It is pleasing to find a relic of earlier times in a palace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to see in' puts G inside HANOVER, the dynasty that ruled Britain from 1714 to 1901; the 'house' is a family, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides the morning-after headache, the word means a custom or thing left over from an earlier time.

clue.text: Worker no longer associated with officer material

indicators.note: no longer associated with means the worker has left the officer's rank, so its letters are taken away

parts.note: a sergeant is a non-commissioned officer in the army, or a police officer
a worker ant is the crossword's usual worker

explanation.surface: A former employee who is no longer mixing with those fit for command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'officer material' reads as one phrase, a person fit for promotion; it splits into the officer and a cloth. 'no longer associated with' removes ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a durable twilled woollen cloth, much used for uniforms.

clue.text: Deliveries no longer available ahead of holidays

indicators.note: ahead of puts the first piece before the second

parts.note: a dish that is off the menu is no longer available
short holidays are called breaks

explanation.surface: The post stops coming just before the vacation.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a delivery is a ball bowled, and this kind spins in from the off side after pitching. The surface suggests parcels.
explanation.definitionFit: They are a type of ball bowled in cricket by a finger spinner.

clue.text: Excess froth precedes upcoming match

indicators.note: precedes puts the froth word before the other piece

parts.note: surf is the foam of breaking waves

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a tie is a match in a knockout competition, as in cup tie

explanation.surface: Too much foam on the beer before the forthcoming game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upcoming' reads as 'forthcoming' but works as 'coming up', giving EIT from a British word for a cup fixture. 'precedes' sets the order.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an overabundance, more than is wanted.

clue.text: Speaker in train held up — they will delay things

indicators.note: in places the speaker inside the turned word
in a down clue held up means the word is written upwards, bottom to top

parts.note: to train a gun on a target is to aim it
an orator is a public speaker

explanation.walkthrough: 'train' is the verb, to point a gun, not the railway kind; 'held up' makes it MIA, and 'in' is the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: They are official suspensions or postponements of activity; the word is a Latin plural.

clue.text: Most stylish Scottish girls received by Court

indicators.note: received by means the girls are taken inside the court's letters

parts.note: Ct is an abbreviation for Court in addresses
lassies is the Scots word for girls

explanation.surface: The best-dressed young Scotswomen are presented to the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'received by' puts LASSIES inside CT; the Court is a street-name abbreviation, not a royal household.
explanation.definitionFit: A superlative synonym: having the greatest elegance.

clue.text: Half-formed desire to be a large-scale creator

parts.note: demi is the prefix for half, so something half-formed is a demi version of it
an urge is a strong desire

explanation.surface: A vague ambition to become a maker on a grand scale.
explanation.definitionFit: In Platonic philosophy this is the being who fashioned the physical universe.

clue.text: Whale beginning to swim up, something oily coming to surface

beginning to picks the opening letter of the word after it

parts.note: taken as written
marg is short for margarine, an oily spread

explanation.walkthrough: 'coming to surface' turns the run S, UP, MARG into the answer read upwards. 'up' looks like a direction but is letters; marg is British shorthand for margarine.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a name for Risso's dolphin, also formerly used for the killer whale.

clue.text: Lamb possibly getting energy from grass, terribly tame

indicators.note: getting, with from, means taking something out of the grass word
from completes getting ... from: the energy letter is taken out of the grass

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet places

parts.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

clue.text: What sounds like Frost's poem

parts.note: rime is hoar frost, the white ice crystals on cold surfaces

explanation.walkthrough: The capital F suggests the poet Robert Frost; it is frozen dew, RIME, and 'What sounds like' asks for a word said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery one is a short piece of verse, so the word can stand for any such composition.

clue.text: Quiet girl offers dull discourse

parts.note: P, for piano, is the music marking for quiet
Rose is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A shy young woman makes tedious conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides ordinary non-verse writing, the word means tedious, commonplace talk.

clue.text: Not hard, to conceal a plan

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not hard' reads as 'easy', but 'Not' removes H from HIDE; the 'a' is then added as written.
